query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_quality
per_column.rationale: Aspect-level assessment of crew service (poor/good/exceptional/mixed) extracted from the review text. It is a distinct experiential driver of overall satisfaction, not the rating itself, and plausibly carries strong predictive signal. Note it partially overlaps the existing numeric 'Staff Service' sub-rating, so incremental leverage beyond the original columns is moderate.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures check-in/gate/ground handling quality (rude_unhelpful/smooth_efficient/etc.). This is a genuine driver that is NOT represented in the original numeric sub-ratings, lies outside overall_rating, and is knowable pre-outcome. Legitimate and largely non-redundant predictor.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Aspect sentiment about catering with informative failure modes (special_meal_failure, out_of_stock). A real satisfaction driver outside the focus. Overlaps the existing 'Food & Beverages' rating but adds finer-grained failure categories, so it retains some incremental predictive value.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How delays/cancellations were handled (well/poorly/partially). Not present in the original columns, a well-known driver of satisfaction, and determined by events during travel (pre-rating). Strong, non-redundant predictor.

per_column.name: post_flight_service_outcome
per_column.rationale: Complaint/issue resolution outcome (resolved/unresolved/ignored). Distinct from the overall score and absent from the original schema. Occurs as part of the experience the reviewer evaluates, not a deterministic function of the rating, so it is a valid predictor with fresh signal.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: A perceived value construct (poor/good/fair). It is a driver rather than a literal restatement of overall_rating, but it duplicates the existing numeric 'Value For Money' sub-rating and is near-collinear with overall satisfaction, so its incremental predictive contribution beyond the original columns is low.

per_column.name: service_consistency_trend
per_column.rationale: Perceived trajectory of service (declining/stable_positive/improving). It adds a temporal-dynamics angle, but the categories bundle valence with trend, making it close to a bare sentiment label; it is a weak/borderline predictor that risks tracking overall sentiment rather than an independent driver.

judge.rationale: The set is a coherent aspect-based feature engineering of the review text, exactly the kind of drivers one wants for explaining/predicting overall satisfaction. All columns lie outside the focus variable, are knowable at/before the time the rating is formed (no post-outcome leakage), and none is a deterministic restatement of overall_rating. Genuine incremental leverage comes from ground_service_quality, disruption_handling_quality, and post_flight_service_outcome, which are absent from the original numeric sub-ratings. Utility is held below high because cabin_crew_quality, food_quality_signal, and especially value_for_money_perception largely duplicate existing numeric sub-ratings (and value-for-money is near-collinear with overall satisfaction), while service_consistency_trend is sentiment-laden and weak. Net: a legitimate, mostly non-trivial predictor set with meaningful but partially redundant added signal.
